title: How to File an FIR in India (Step-by-Step Guide)
summary: A practical walkthrough on registering a First Information Report (FIR) under Section 173 of BNSS 2023, knowing what details to include, and what to do if police refuse registration.

steps.heading: Identify the Cognizable Offence
steps.text: Ensure the crime involves a cognizable offence (e.g. theft, assault, robbery, cyber fraud). If minor, police will log an NCR instead.

steps.heading: Visit the Police Station or Lodge Zero FIR
steps.text: Go to the nearest police station having territorial jurisdiction. In emergency or out-of-station scenarios, request a Zero FIR.

steps.heading: Provide Oral or Written Statement
steps.text: Narrate the facts clearly: Date, Time, Exact Location, Accused Name/Description, Witnesses, and Stolen Property details. The police officer will write it down.

steps.heading: Verify and Sign the FIR Copy
steps.text: Read the written FIR statement carefully. Ensure no facts were omitted or distorted. Sign the statement.

steps.heading: Obtain Free Stamped Copy of FIR
steps.text: Under BNSS Section 173(2), collect the official stamped copy of the FIR with the unique FIR Number immediately, completely free of charge.

warnings: Never give false or misleading statements in an FIR. Filing a false FIR is punishable under Section 248 of BNS 2023.
Do not leave the station without your official free stamped copy of the FIR.

faqs.q: What if the Police Station Superintendent refuses to register the FIR?
faqs.a: Send your complaint in writing via registered post to the Superintendent of Police (SP) under BNSS Section 173(4), or file a direct complaint before the Judicial Magistrate.

title: What to Do After an Online Financial Fraud
summary: Immediate critical actions to take within the 'Golden Hour' after suffering UPI, net-banking, or credit card fraud in India.

steps.heading: Call National Cyber Crime Helpline 1930
steps.text: Dial 1930 immediately. Provide your mobile number, bank name, account number, and transaction UTR details to trigger financial asset freezing.

steps.heading: Lodge Online Complaint on cybercrime.gov.in
steps.text: Fill out the official complaint form on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal. Attach screenshots of transaction SMS, bank statements, and fraud links.

steps.heading: Notify Your Bank Branch
steps.text: Submit a formal written notification to your bank manager within 3 days. Under RBI zero-liability rules, prompt reporting protects you against unauthorized electronic banking losses.

warnings: Do not delay calling 1930. The first 1 to 2 hours are crucial before fraudsters transfer money across multiple wallet layers.

title: How Anticipatory Bail Works in India
summary: Understanding pre-arrest protection under Section 482 BNSS, eligible offences, court criteria, and conditions imposed.

steps.heading: Evaluate Apprehension of Arrest
steps.text: Consult a legal advocate if there is reasonable ground to believe a non-bailable FIR or false complaint is imminent.

steps.heading: File Application in Sessions Court or High Court
steps.text: Draft an anticipatory bail application highlighting lack of flight risk, cooperation with investigation, and bogus allegations.

steps.heading: Interim Protection & Final Hearing
steps.text: The judge may grant interim protection against arrest while calling for police status reports before passing final orders.

warnings: Anticipatory bail does not mean you can evade police inquiry; you are mandated to join investigation whenever called.
